inspectedLocal.caption: The Tower of Winds was built as a combination of clock, sundial and astrological calendar by Andronikos of Kyrrhos, according to Vitruvius.
inspectedLocal.inspection: 2008 original inspected: tall octagonal Pentelic marble body, irregular large block courses, winged wind reliefs in upper frieze, small later high vent, door grille/porch column stumps, three base steps and southern cylindrical annex fragment. Neighbouring ruins/stairs and detached blocks not included.

focusedSupplements.caption: Aerides Tower, Tower of the Winds, in the Plaka quarter, Athens, Greece.
focusedSupplements.inspection: 2009 original inspected: surviving two stump columns on north porch, missing pediment/porch roof, deep rectangular closed grilled door, wind relief and cornice/lion water spouts; no restoration of full porch claimed.

sources.inspection: Primary architectural investigator Hermann J.Kienast2013 text read: regular octagon side about3.25m; three base steps; main wall almost9m, variable course heights and three narrow binder courses; frieze of eight rightward flying winged winds;24 marble roof slabs/three per side forming eight-sided pyramid, clay joint-cover tiles today; surviving capital fragment; three of four porch column stumps and missing pediments; southern round annex badly damaged. These survive-state descriptions override restoring full porches in initial batch wording.

Aerial inspected: octagonal roof with radial joint covers, two northern porch remains and low southern round annex, distinct from archaeological ruins and high surrounding streets. Roof displacement not treated as ground anchor.

scopeCorrection: Surviving porch steps and column stumps; no full pediments/columns restored. Southern reservoir is broken/open.
limitations: Surviving exterior from selected2008 and focused2009/2014/2017/2022 originals, primary architectural investigator text and mapped/aerial controls. No photographic pixels redistributed. Side length~3.25m and main wall almost9m guide scale; source map approximate12.5m top. Exact elevations, sculpture contours/poses, slab/cornice profiles, blocked openings and individual damaged courses remain estimates.

Two north entrance porches represented as current stepped platforms, three stump columns and wall scars; missing pediments/full columns not restored. Southern reservoir annex is broken/open, not complete historical cylinder. Original bronze Triton vane absent. Modern grilles retained approximately; interiors, water mechanism, detached fragments/furniture, site retaining walls and neighbouring ruins/stairs excluded.
Independent terrain remains unchanged; archaeological excavation cut may not be resolved in coarse host DEM and geographic readiness requires current contact review. Footprint replacement disabled.
